defect.evidence_quote: We thus hold that, if police initiate interrogation after a defendant’s assertion, at an arraignment or similar proceeding, of his right to counsel, any waiver of the defendant’s right to counsel for that police-initiated interrogation is invalid.
defect.problem: 'post-appointment' mischaracterizes the Jackson trigger: the rule turns on the defendant's assertion/request of the right to counsel at arraignment, not on counsel actually being appointed (in Bladel the appointment notice had not even reached the firm when police interrogated).
defect.proposed_fix: Replace 'post-appointment' with 'after the defendant asserts/requests the right to counsel at arraignment'.

reasons: Core proposition supported at *636 (pin-636): a police-initiated waiver after the defendant asserts counsel at arraignment is invalid; the 'overruled by Montejo v. Louisiana (2009)' tag matches the lake edge (556 U.S. 778, field_ii overruled).

The modifier 'post-appointment' is imprecise against the opinion's trigger language ('assertion... of his right to counsel') and against the page's own Issue section ('after the defendant has requested counsel'); substance is otherwise correct.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Tighten 'post-appointment' to 'after the defendant requests/asserts the right to counsel at arraignment' to match the opinion's trigger.
